newsitem.title: JAPAN: INTERVIEW-Sony unit mulls raising PlayStation output.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Sony unit mulls raising PlayStation output.

text.p: Sony Computer Entertainment, a unit of electronics giant Sony Corp, says it is mulling raising production of its game console PlayStation amid booming sales.
"We are currently considering further increasing production of PlayStation to meet strong demand," president Teruhisa Tokunaka told Reuters in a recent interview.
The company currently produces 1.5 million units of PlayStation per month, more than double the monthly output of 70,000 units a year ago.
The main reason behind the success of the 32-bit game machine was the support from game software makers which produced attractive software which run on PlayStation, Tokunaka said.
He said PlayStation's wide variety of software could create a much larger market than that of arch rival Nintendo Co Ltd's 64-bit machine Nintendo 64.
The diversity in software has helped increase video game players, Tokunaka said.
"Game machines have traditionally been seen as something only young boys play with. We have been aiming to make our PlayStation also enjoyable for adults and females," he said.
Tokunaka declined to comment on what the company envisages as the next-generation game machine.
Riding on the strong sales, industry analysts expect Sony Computer to eventually topple Nintendo, known as the king of the home video game market.
Sony Computer said that, as of end-March, worldwide shipments of PlayStation totalled 13.5 million units since the game was first launched in Japan in December 1994.
The company expects to ship 18 million units worldwide in the current business year which ends March 31, up from estimated shipments of 8.9 million the previous year.
Global net sales of PlayStations and its software are forecast to reach 650 billion yen ($5.60 billion) this business year, up from 400 billion yen ($3.44 billion) a year earlier, Sony Computer said.
Nintendo said on Tuesday that sales of its mainstay 64-bit game machine, Nintendo 64, and related software were expected to total 314 billion yen ($2.70 billion) in 1997/98.
The figure is sharply higher than 178.4 billion yen ($1.53 billion) in 1996/97, but is still far behind PlayStation's sales.
Nintendo plans to ship 12 million units of its 64-bit game machine globally this business year, up from 6.12 million in the previous year. ($1=116 yen)
